To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the activation of oncogenic pathways can be identified by a combination of methods including gene expression profiling, proteomics, and immunohistochemistry; (ii) the activation of specific oncogenic pathways is correlated with specific clinical and pathologic characteristics, suggesting the potential for pathway-specific therapy; (iii) oncogenic pathways can interact with each other, suggesting the possibility of combination therapy.
the combination of DNA microarray and pathway analyses provides an effective strategy for identifying potential therapeutic strategies in cancer.
molecular profiling of tumours can be used to link pathway deregulations with potential therapeutic strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the pathways that are deregulated during tumourigenesis and the development of therapeutic strategies to target these pathways in cancer.
the identification and characterisation of novel therapeutic targets for cancer treatment.
the identification of novel therapeutic targets in the treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the complexity of cancer is reflected by the complexity of the pathways that are deregulated and that these pathways are potential therapeutic targets.
, while molecular profiling has not yet led to a major change in the treatment of cancer, it has provided a new way of looking at cancer, and the results obtained so far have been very exciting.
the molecular profiling of cancers has the potential to provide the basis for a personalized approach to cancer therapy.

we have identified a number of oncogenic pathways in a variety of tumours and have linked this to the development of potential therapeutic approaches.
the complexity of the cancer genome can be reduced to a few pathways that can be targeted with a few drugs.
it is important to understand the molecular pathways in cancer cells and to develop strategies for targeting the pathways.

the use of molecular profiling in the clinical setting will be essential for the development of effective personalized cancer therapy.
